The first such mention occurs in Henry V (Act 1 Scene 2), where the Archbishop of Canterbury cites it directly during the Salic-law debate: “For in the book of Numbers is it writ…” (citing Num. 27:8).  

No earlier canonical book (Genesis–Leviticus) is ever named by title anywhere in the plays; later books such as Job or the Gospels appear only after Numbers in both canonical sequence and dramatic chronology. (While a few early comedies contain possible puns on “numbers,” they do not constitute an explicit named citation of the biblical book itself.)  

Thus the required pair is Numbers / Henry V.
